chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) would, if something from the night was missed by him, make it up during the day; and if something from the day was missed by him, he would make it up the next day, or on Friday, or within the month. And when matters accumulated upon him, he would make them up in the month of Sha'ban until his work for the entire year was complete.

key_terms.الشَّهْرِ: The month (referring to the lunar month, likely Ramadan or generally any month)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.عَمَلُ السَّنَةِ: The work of the year (referring to the total accumulated prayers/acts of worship for the year)
key_terms.قَضَاهُ: He made it up (compensated for a missed act of worship)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn handle missed prayers and what is the significance of making them up in Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical piety of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), demonstrating a balanced approach to *qada* (making up missed prayers) that accommodates life's demands without neglecting spiritual duties. By consolidating accumulated prayers in Sha'ban, he exemplified the scholarly principle of maintaining consistent annual worship (*kamil*) while allowing flexibility for individual circumstances. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on both the obligation of fulfilling missed duties and the ease (*taysir*) granted to believers in their worship.
